import type {
  DocumentTranslationContext,
  DocumentTranslationClientOptionalParams,
} from "./api/index.js";
import { createDocumentTranslation } from "./api/index.js";
import type {
  StartTranslationDetails,
  TranslationStatus,
  DocumentStatus,
  SupportedFileFormats,
  FileFormatType,
} from "../models/models.js";
import type { PagedAsyncIterableIterator } from "../static-helpers/pagingHelpers.js";
import {
  getSupportedFormats,
  listDocumentStatuses,
  cancelTranslation,
  getTranslationStatus,
  getDocumentStatus,
  listTranslationStatuses,
  startTranslation,
} from "./api/operations.js";
import type {
  GetSupportedFormatsOptionalParams,
  ListDocumentStatusesOptionalParams,
  CancelTranslationOptionalParams,
  GetTranslationStatusOptionalParams,
  GetDocumentStatusOptionalParams,
  ListTranslationStatusesOptionalParams,
  StartTranslationOptionalParams,
} from "./api/options.js";
import type { KeyCredential, TokenCredential } from "@azure/core-auth";
import type { PollerLike, OperationState } from "@azure/core-lro";
import type { Pipeline } from "@azure/core-rest-pipeline";

export type { DocumentTranslationClientOptionalParams } from "./api/documentTranslationContext.js";

/**
 * Client for the Azure AI Document Translation service, used to translate batches of documents stored in Azure Blob Storage.
 */
export class DocumentTranslationClient {
  private _client: DocumentTranslationContext;
  /** The pipeline used by this client to make requests */
  public readonly pipeline: Pipeline;

  /**
   * Creates an instance of {@link DocumentTranslationClient}.
   *
   * @param endpointParam - The Document Translation endpoint, for example `https://<resource-name>.cognitiveservices.azure.com`.
   * @param credential - A key credential or token credential used to authenticate requests to the service.
   * @param options - Options used to configure the client.
   */
  constructor(
    endpointParam: string,
    credential: KeyCredential | TokenCredential,
    options: DocumentTranslationClientOptionalParams = {},
  ) {
    this._client = createDocumentTranslation(endpointParam, credential, options);
    this.pipeline = this._client.pipeline;
  }

  /**
   * The list of supported formats supported by the Document Translation
   * service.
   * The list includes the common file extension, as well as the
   * content-type if using the upload API.
   */
  getSupportedFormats(
    typeParam: FileFormatType,
    options: GetSupportedFormatsOptionalParams = { requestOptions: {} },
  ): Promise<SupportedFileFormats> {
    return getSupportedFormats(this._client, typeParam, options);
  }

  /**
   * Returns the status for all documents in a batch document translation request.
   *
   *
   * If the number of documents in the response exceeds our paging limit,
   * server-side paging is used.
   * Paginated responses indicate a partial result and
   * include a continuation token in the response. The absence of a continuation
   * token means that no additional pages are available.
   *
   * top, skip
   * and maxPageSize options can be used to specify a number of results to
   * return and an offset for the collection.
   *
   * top indicates the total
   * number of records the user wants to be returned across all pages.
   * skip
   * indicates the number of records to skip from the list of document status held
   * by the server based on the sorting method specified.  By default, we sort by
   * descending start time.
   * maxPageSize is the maximum items returned in a page.
   * If more items are requested via top (or top is not specified and there are
   * more items to be returned), @nextLink will contain the link to the next page.
   *
   *
   * The orderBy option can be used to sort the returned list (ex:
   * orderBy: ["createdDateTimeUtc asc"] or orderBy: ["createdDateTimeUtc
   * desc"]).
   * The default sorting is descending by createdDateTimeUtc.
   * The statuses,
   * documentIds, createdAfter, and createdBefore options can be used to filter the
   * returned list (ex: statuses: ["Succeeded", "Cancelled"] will only return
   * succeeded and cancelled documents).
   * createdAfter and createdBefore can be used
   * combined or separately to specify a range of datetime to filter the returned
   * list by.
   * The supported filtering options are (statuses, documentIds,
   * createdAfter, createdBefore).
   *
   * When both top
   * and skip are included, the server should first apply skip and then top on
   * the collection.
   * Note: If the server can't honor top and/or skip, the server
   * must return an error to the client informing about it instead of just ignoring
   * the query options.
   * This reduces the risk of the client making assumptions about
   * the data returned.
   */
  listDocumentStatuses(
    translationId: string,
    options: ListDocumentStatusesOptionalParams = { requestOptions: {} },
  ): PagedAsyncIterableIterator<DocumentStatus> {
    return listDocumentStatuses(this._client, translationId, options);
  }

  /**
   * Cancel a currently processing or queued translation.
   * A translation will not be
   * cancelled if it is already completed or failed or cancelling. A bad request
   * will be returned.
   * All documents that have completed translation will not be
   * cancelled and will be charged.
   * All pending documents will be cancelled if
   * possible.
   */
  cancelTranslation(
    translationId: string,
    options: CancelTranslationOptionalParams = { requestOptions: {} },
  ): Promise<TranslationStatus> {
    return cancelTranslation(this._client, translationId, options);
  }

  /**
   * Returns the status for a document translation request.
   * The status includes the
   * overall request status, as well as the status for documents that are being
   * translated as part of that request.
   */
  getTranslationStatus(
    translationId: string,
    options: GetTranslationStatusOptionalParams = { requestOptions: {} },
  ): Promise<TranslationStatus> {
    return getTranslationStatus(this._client, translationId, options);
  }

  /**
   * Returns the translation status for a specific document based on the request Id
   * and document Id.
   */
  getDocumentStatus(
    translationId: string,
    documentId: string,
    options: GetDocumentStatusOptionalParams = { requestOptions: {} },
  ): Promise<DocumentStatus> {
    return getDocumentStatus(this._client, translationId, documentId, options);
  }

  /**
   * Returns a list of batch requests submitted and the status for each
   * request.
   * This list only contains batch requests submitted by the user (based on
   * the resource).
   *
   * If the number of requests exceeds our paging limit,
   * server-side paging is used. Paginated responses indicate a partial result and
   * include a continuation token in the response.
   * The absence of a continuation
   * token means that no additional pages are available.
   *
   * top, skip
   * and maxPageSize options can be used to specify a number of results to
   * return and an offset for the collection.
   *
   * top indicates the total
   * number of records the user wants to be returned across all pages.
   * skip
   * indicates the number of records to skip from the list of batches based on the
   * sorting method specified.  By default, we sort by descending start
   * time.
   * maxPageSize is the maximum items returned in a page.  If more items are
   * requested via top (or top is not specified and there are more items to be
   * returned), @nextLink will contain the link to the next page.
   *
   *
   * The orderBy option can be used to sort the returned list (ex:
   * orderBy: ["createdDateTimeUtc asc"] or orderBy: ["createdDateTimeUtc
   * desc"]).
   * The default sorting is descending by createdDateTimeUtc.
   * The statuses,
   * translationIds, createdAfter, and createdBefore options can be used to filter the
   * returned list (ex: statuses: ["Succeeded", "Cancelled"] will only return
   * succeeded and cancelled operations).
   * createdAfter and createdBefore can be used
   * combined or separately to specify a range of datetime to filter the returned
   * list by.
   * The supported filtering options are (statuses, translationIds,
   * createdAfter, createdBefore).
   *
   * The server honors
   * the values specified by the client. However, clients must be prepared to handle
   * responses that contain a different page size or contain a continuation token.
   *
   *
   * When both top and skip are included, the server should first apply
   * skip and then top on the collection.
   * Note: If the server can't honor top
   * and/or skip, the server must return an error to the client informing about it
   * instead of just ignoring the query options.
   * This reduces the risk of the client
   * making assumptions about the data returned.
   */
  listTranslationStatuses(
    options: ListTranslationStatusesOptionalParams = { requestOptions: {} },
  ): PagedAsyncIterableIterator<TranslationStatus> {
    return listTranslationStatuses(this._client, options);
  }

  /**
   * Use this API to submit a bulk (batch) translation request to the Document
   * Translation service.
   * Each request can contain multiple documents and must
   * contain a source and destination container for each document.
   *
   * The
   * prefix and suffix filter (if supplied) are used to filter folders. The prefix
   * is applied to the subpath after the container name.
   *
   * Glossaries /
   * Translation memory can be included in the request and are applied by the
   * service when the document is translated.
   *
   * If the glossary is
   * invalid or unreachable during translation, an error is indicated in the
   * document status.
   * If a file with the same name already exists at the
   * destination, it will be overwritten. The targetUrl for each target language
   * must be unique.
   */
  startTranslation(
    body: StartTranslationDetails,
    options: StartTranslationOptionalParams = { requestOptions: {} },
  ): PollerLike<OperationState<TranslationStatus>, TranslationStatus> {
    return startTranslation(this._client, body, options);
  }
}

omissions.explanation: The exported restorePoller function reconstructs a poller from serialized state, selects an operation deserializer and expected statuses through a route map, permits an optional response-body processor, and passes restoration state and API version to getLongRunningPoller. Whether this helper is handwritten or generated, and whether callers can reach it through the package's public exports, is not established by the supplied evidence.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: Candidate only: this nontrivial helper lives in src/documentTranslation/ rather than an explicitly named generated/ directory and has no generated header, but neither signal proves it was handwritten; a generator could also emit this operation-specific restoration code. A generated counterpart or generation history is needed before counting it.

limitations: Coverage is partial: five distinct source paths of 61 eligible files are supplied, out of 120 discovered files. Single-document operations/client/context, model serializers, multipart handling, polling/paging helpers and stream/error-body implementations are excluded. Empty findings mean no established handwritten customizations in this bounded evidence, not no package customizations.

All five evidence items have unknown provenance. This is a modular src layout without supplied generated counterparts, overlay differences, explicit handwritten markers or a generator ownership map. The frozen JavaScript guideline leaves this layout's provenance unresolved; exported classes/functions, missing generated headers and LRO helper names are not sufficient proof of handwriting.

createDocumentTranslation visibly builds an endpoint with /translator unless options.endpoint is supplied, configures user-agent/logging options, supplies default Cognitive Services scopes and an Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header name, and carries options.serviceVersion into apiVersion. These normal client-factory/auth-configuration bodies have no affirmative handwritten signal. The imported getClient implementation is absent, so credential handling is not independently assessed.

The operation module contains ordinary request construction, expected-status checks and model serialization/deserialization. List methods call buildPagedAsyncIterator with value/nextLink and a configured or 2026-03-01 API version; startTranslation calls getLongRunningPoller with operation-location, initial-send callback, expected 202/200/201 responses, abort signal and update interval. Generated paging/LRO behavior is expressly not a customization, and the helper bodies are excluded.

DocumentTranslationClient constructs its context, exposes that context's pipeline and forwards method arguments to operation functions. Wrapping modular operation functions does not by itself establish a handwritten client or convenience customization, and no altered return shaping or additional local polling strategy is visible in those forwarding methods.

restorePoller visibly reads serialized config, requires initialRequestUrl/requestMethod, chooses a supplied processResponseBody or URL/method-selected deserializer, extracts api-version and delegates restoration to getLongRunningPoller with restoreFrom and resource-location metadata. Its local map contains POST /document/batches with the start-translation deserializer and 202/200/201 statuses; sourceOperation is used in diagnostic names rather than as the dispatch selector. This is a concrete restoration candidate, but not proven handwritten or additional to generator output.

The restore helper's path matcher compares path components from the end and prefers the longest matching configured candidate; it is not a demonstrated exact-path or client-membership validator. With a caller deserializer and no map match, expectedStatuses defaults to an empty array. No runtime correctness, resume compatibility, polling-state validation or missing helper behavior is inferred from the comments or types.

The single-document README sample uses multipart input and a readableStreamBody result, but samples are not implementation evidence. Package core-lro dependencies and exported subpaths likewise do not establish customization, and the relevant source implementations are not supplied.

Source package metadata reports 1.0.1 while latestRelease reports 1.0.0. This review preserves the frozen identity and metadata without verifying released artifacts, regeneration, network execution or the behavior of excluded dependencies.

The analyst supplied zero proposals, so there are no decisions to accept, revise, reject, or mark inconclusive. The one possible omission is inconclusive and uncounted, not an AI-verified or human-verified customization.

All five supplied source evidence fragments have kind unknown and refer to five distinct paths. No generated/ counterpart, generated-vs-source diff, customization script, or generation history was supplied; ordinary API-version, authentication, paging, and startTranslation poller code cannot be classified as handwritten solely because it performs those behaviors.

The collector metadata reports partial coverage: 120 discovered files, 61 eligible files, five captured files, and ten explicitly listed skipped paths. These counts are not an exhaustive inventory or proof that uncaptured files lack customizations.

The package metadata lists documentTranslation exports but does not itself establish whether restorePoller is re-exported by the entry point; public activation and runtime effects of the potential omission remain unverified. Human overrides remain authoritative over any AI assessment.
